newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shares end higher, players await news.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shares end higher, players await news.

text.p: Brazilian stocks ended slightly higher in tepid trade, as investors waited for news on the political fallout from a cash-for-votes scandal and amid caution ahead of Tuesday's Fed Reserve policy meeting, brokers said.
"The market is calm," said one local dealer. "It's waiting for more news."
The Sao Paulo bourse's Bovespa index of 48 most-traded shares moved up a slight 0.06 percent to end at 10,506 points on moderate trade of 495 million reais ($467 million).
Individual stocks moved on the release of first-quarter results for some companies but most trade was stable due to a lack of market-moving news, brokers said.

They said investors have mostly taken positions and are awaiting the outcome of Tuesday's U.S. Fed meeting or possible repercussions from an alleged congressional voting-buying scheme that one newspaper said may involve the government.
"The market was calm, working within a certain normalcy," one broker said.
Among the day's leaders was Petrobras common, which shot up 6.32 percent to end at 185.00 reais.
